items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I remember John Collins, the banjo [guitar] player, started out playing banjo.

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s interesting. You know I guess you can go to college now and you can take the business of music, you know?

Yeah, that’s a good thing. Because they no longer do, like when Milt and I came along, in high school, there was like it is in college now. I mean they had these bands and every high school had a band in Chicago and I remember the professor who taught music in Phillips High School where Milt went. It was just perfect. You’d walk in and you’d get private lessons from him plus rehearsing, you know playing with the band and everything, and it developed some great musicians. And a lot of them would walk in and didn’t…

Well a lot of the people we’ve talked to have talked about their great high school experience and it’s amazing the congregation of people that were in Chicago for instance, the famous names that all came out of there in that time period.
